title: On Handling the matter without advice
subtitle: 服务职业 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 服务职业（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·服务行业与职业）
meta: 主题语境：服务职业（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·服务行业与职业）　|　核心词汇：handle　|　正文 348 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 handle 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1964 the engineer ① handled the matter without advice with great care, and every worker in the workshop said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three years on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the engineer ② handles the matter without advice on the same day without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ handle the matter without advice at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ handled the matter without advice before — a line in the manual for April 1958 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Handling the matter without advice with great care, the engineer said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the lever at the far bench, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ handle the glassware as if it were gold on the same day, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Handle the glassware as if it were gold at once and never mention it again.

By 1971 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the manual, and a new worker from the next workshop ⑧ handles the glassware as if it were gold with great care every year without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the bench, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ handled the matter without advice again when nobody else would.

⑩ To handle the matter without advice, my mother said in 1976, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the workshop remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the workshop forgets, somebody handles the matter without advice on the same day again and somebody must handle the matter without advice with great care all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 处理（一般过去式 handled the matter without advice：1964 年工程师头一回这样做，小心翼翼地）
B. v. 处理（一般现在 handles the matter without advice：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 处理（不定式 to handle the matter without advice：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 处理（过去完成时 had handled the matter without advice：1958 年四月的说明书上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 处理（动名词 handling the matter without advice 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 搬弄（handle the glassware as if it were gold：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去搬弄把那些玻璃器皿当宝贝似的搬弄）
G. v. 搬弄（handle the glassware as if it were gold：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 处理（后段两处：新来的工人照例 handles the glassware as if it were gold，而母亲又一次 handled the matter without advice）

answers.why: handle 意为“处理”，1964 年工程师小心翼翼地处理不请教任何人就把事情处理了，那是车间里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 handled。
handle 意为“处理”，自那以后工程师当天就把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 handles。
handle 意为“处理”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯处理不请教任何人就把事情处理了”，此处为不定式 to handle the matter without advice。
handle 意为“处理”，说明书里 四月 那行字说明早在 1971 年之前就有人处理过，故用过去完成时 had handled。
handle 意为“处理”，工程师说“处理不请教任何人就把事情处理了这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 handling the matter without advice 作主语。
handle 意为“搬弄”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去搬弄把那些玻璃器皿当宝贝似的搬弄”，should ever 之后用原形 handle the glassware as if it were gold。
handle 意为“搬弄”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻搬弄把那些玻璃器皿当宝贝似的搬弄（handle the glassware as if it were gold at once），以后再也不要提起。
handle 意为“处理”，新来的工人每个年头都照例搬弄把那些玻璃器皿当宝贝似的搬弄，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 handles。
handle 意为“处理”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次小心翼翼地处理不请教任何人就把事情处理了，用一般过去式 handled 叙述。
handle 意为“处理”，结尾那句是母亲 1976 年的话：要处理不请教任何人就把事情处理了，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和车间记住的那一件。

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 handle 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1964 the engineer handled the matter without advice with great care, and nobody in the workshop forgot it.
Even now the engineer handles the matter without advice on the same day whenever the workshop asks.
Handling the matter without advice with great care, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever handle the glassware as if it were gold on the same day, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new worker from the next workshop handles the glassware as if it were gold with great care every year, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother handled the matter without advice again, and the workshop remembered that half.
